title: Cap. VI Arg. 2: 2 Tim. 1:9; Prosper — this grace barred by no evil merits, bought by no good
pass_a_gloss: Thus speaks the Apostle, He has saved us, and called us with a holy calling, not from our works, but from his purpose and grace. 2 Tim. 1:9. This grace is barred by no evil merits, is obtained by no good ones, Prosper, Response to the Chapters of the Gauls, 8. This grace makes that we will, makes that we do, makes that we believe. This grace works good wills in men, Augustine, On the Grace of Christ, chapter 29.
pass_b_english: So Paul: he saved us and called us with a holy calling — not from our works, but from his purpose and grace (2 Tim. 1:9). Prosper (Response to the Gallican Chapters, 8): no evil merits bar this grace, no good ones purchase it. Augustine (On the Grace of Christ, ch. 29): it makes us will, makes us act, makes us believe, and works good wills in men.
source_text: Sic loquitur Apostolus, Servavit nos, et vocavit vocatione sancta, non ex operibus nostris, sed ex suo proposito et gratia. 2 Tim. i. 9. Haec gratia nullis malis meritis arcetur, nullis bonis impetratur, Prosper, ad Cap. Gallor. resp. 8. Haec gratia facit ut velimus, facit ut faciamus, facit ut credamus. Haec gratia bonas voluntates in hominibus operatur, Augustinus, De grat. Christi, cap. 29.
